records.title: Fact Check: Ignat Shchetinin And Sammy Scott Piatt Not ...
records.retrieval_query: Clackamas County Circuit Court docket search for Ignat Shchetinin arson charge 2020

passages.P2: Were Ignat Shchetinin and Sammy Scott Piatt charged with arson in connection with wildfires raging in Clackamas County, Oregon? No, that's not true. While two men have been charged with arson, the charges are not related to the wildfires in northwestern Oregon. They were charged in separate incidents with arson -- one related to lighting leaves on fire that were quickly extinguished and the other for starting a fire in a store to win someone's attention.
passages.P3: The implication that Shechetinin and Piatt's arrest were connected to the wildfires appeared in a post (archived here) shared on Facebook Sept. 13, 2020. With two mugshots below it, the post read:
passages.P4: > Nope, no arson arrests in Clackamas County. Oh look...here's a couple recent mugshots. I wouldn't be surprised to see more 🤬
passages.P5: This is what the post looked like on Facebook at the time of writing:
passages.P6: *(Source: Facebook screenshot taken on Mon Sep 14 15:47:50 2020 UTC)*
passages.P7: While the post does not specifically state that the arson charges were related to wildfires, the timing of the post and the comments below it suggested that. The same is true of other posts similar to the one posted by Terraka Mishler.
passages.P8: Here is another, just with different wording, and commenters have pointed out that they had nothing to do with the fires -- to which the poster replied, asking about one of the charged men's alleged possession of body armour at the time of his arrest.
passages.P9: The men charged are Ignat Shchetinin, 37 and Sammy Scott Piatt, 53.
passages.P10: Shchetinin's charged were described in the following Sept. 12 statement by the Clackamas County Sheriff's Office:
passages.P11:
> On Labor Day (Monday, Sept. 7), Clackamas County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to a report that a suspect had ignited clothing articles on a merchandise rack at the Clackamas Fred Meyer (16301 SE 82nd Dr., Clackamas).
>
> Deputies obtained images of the suspect from store cameras.
>
> On Sept. 11, deputies spotted the suspect -- later identified as Ignat Shchetinin, 37 -- on Hwy. 212 and 82nd Dr. in Clackamas, near the same Fred Meyer.
>
> When contacted, Mr. Shchetinin confessed to interntionally igniting the clothing inside the Fred Meyer, using a purple Bic-style lighter. He told deputies he did this to get the attention of a person who wouldn't speak with him.
>
> Deputies also discovered Mr. Shchetinin possessed a baggie of methamphetamine.
>
> Ignat Shchetinin was transported to Clackamas County Jail on charges including:
>
> * ORS.164.325 - ARSON I
> * ORS.475.894-1 - PCS-METH
>
> Bail was set at $250,000..."
passages.P12: For Piatt, the Oregon City Police Department released this on their Facebook page:
passages.P13: As searched here, Piatt was on probation at the time for felony possession of body armour and a methamphetmine drug charge.
passages.P14: According to a story posted Sept. 12 by KOIN, a CBS station in Oregon, the arson charges sparked much speculation about some connection to the wildfires in the area:
passages.P15: > ...Word quickly spread on social media, adding fuel to rumors that at least some of the fires popping up in rural areas around the county may be the result of arson. According to authorities, though, that's not the case."
passages.P16: There have reportedly been at least four people arrested for arsons tied to the wildfires, but these arrests and suggestions that extremists on either side were to blame have so far proven baseless, according to the FBI and this story in The New York Times from Sept. 10.

records.title: Clackamas County: 2 arson arrests not connected to wildfires
records.retrieval_query: Clackamas County Circuit Court docket search for Ignat Shchetinin arson charge 2020

passages.P1: Ignat Shchetinin (left) and Sammy Piatt (right) were both arrested on arson charges Friday, Sept. 11, 2020 in separate cases (Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office)
passages.P2: Both suspects were booked for separate crimes Friday, September 11
passages.P6: CLACKAMAS COUNTY, Ore. (KOIN) — Law enforcement agencies in Clackamas County released details Saturday about two recent arson arrests, debunking rumors that they may have been connected to wildfires in the area.
passages.P7: Sammy Piatt, 53, and Ignat Shchetinin, 37, were both arrested and booked Friday on charges that included arson. Word quickly spread on social media, adding fuel to rumors that at least some of the fires popping up in rural areas around the county may be the result of arson. According to authorities, though, that’s not the case.
passages.P8: Ignat Shchetinin, 37, is accused of setting clothes on fire at a Fred Meyer (Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office)
passages.P9: Shchetinin is accused of lighting clothes on fire at the Clackamas Fred Meyer on Monday. Clackamas County deputies used surveillance videos from the store to identify the suspect, and allegedly found Shchetinin near the same store on Friday.
passages.P10: Police said he confessed to lighting the clothes on fire using a Bic-style lighter to “get the attention of a person who wouldn’t speak with him.” Deputies also allegedly found a baggie of methamphetamine on Shchetinin. He’s now being held on $250,000 bail.
passages.P11: Sammy Piatt, 53, is accused of lighting a pile of leaves on fire near a building on Sept. 11, 2020 in Oregon City (Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office)
passages.P12: Meanwhile, Oregon City Police officers arrested Piatt near the Clackamas County Community Solutions building at 112 11th Street in Oregon City, after he allegedly set a pile of leaves on fire. One officer put the fire out while another detained Piatt, according to police. The fire was about ten feet from the building and did not cause any damage.
passages.P13: Piatt, who police say is homeless, was booked on charges of second degree arson and a probation violation.

records.retrieval_query: What court records or charging documents show arson charges against Ignat Shchetinin and Sammy Scott Piatt?

passages.P1: # Arson Charges and Defense in Federal Fire Investigations
passages.P4: Federal arson charges depend on the property's federal connection, the cause of the fire, and proof of the required mental state.
passages.P5: A wildfire alone does not establish guilt. Prosecutors must connect the accused to the alleged ignition and prove the charged statute's elements using reliable evidence.
passages.P6: ## 1. When Federal Fire Investigations Lead to Arson Charges
passages.P7: Federal jurisdiction depends on the property and statute. A fire on federal land does not satisfy every arson provision.
passages.P8: ### Federal Property and Public Land Offenses
passages.P9: 18 U.S.C. § 844(f)(1) covers malicious fire damage or attempted damage to federal property or property of certain federally assisted institutions.
passages.P10: Section 1855 separately prohibits willful, unauthorized burning of vegetation on specified federal and tribal lands. Land records and fire boundaries help establish which statute applies.
passages.P11: ### Interstate Commerce and Special Federal Jurisdiction
passages.P12: Section 844(i) covers property used in interstate or foreign commerce or activity affecting commerce. Under *Jones v. United States*, a noncommercial owner-occupied home does not qualify solely through utilities or insurance.
passages.P13: Section 81 applies within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction defined by 18 U.S.C. § 7. Federal ownership alone is insufficient.
passages.P14: ## 2. Evidence Used in Federal Arson Investigations
passages.P15: Fire-origin findings must be distinguished from proof of the accused's conduct and intent.
passages.P16:
| Evidence | Issue to Examine |
| --- | --- |
| Origin-and-cause reports | Ignition location and competing explanations |
| Scene photographs and fire patterns | Fire spread and scene alteration |
| Debris testing and laboratory reports | Ignition materials and analytical limits |
| Surveillance, phone, and location data | Actions and chronology |
| Witness statements | Observation and consistency |
| Land records and custody logs | Jurisdiction and evidence integrity |
passages.P18: * Issue to ExamineIgnition location and competing explanations
passages.P20: * Issue to ExamineFire spread and scene alteration
passages.P22: * Issue to ExamineIgnition materials and analytical limits
passages.P28: * Issue to ExamineJurisdiction and evidence integrity
passages.P29: ### Fire Origin, Ignition Sources, and Forensic Reports
passages.P30: NFPA 921 guides systematic analysis of ignition sources, fire patterns, and evidence handling; it is not a criminal statute. Suppression efforts and disturbed debris may limit findings.
passages.P31: ### Witness Statements, Digital Records, and Physical Evidence
passages.P32: Witness accounts and device records require comparison with the physical timeline.
passages.P33: On October 9, 2026, DOJ announced a criminal complaint against Rodney Ameile Saba concerning the Bouquet Fire, which burned about 1,048 acres of federal land.
passages.P34: U.S. Forest Service investigators concluded that fireworks probably caused the fire after excluding alternative ignition sources. The allegations do not establish guilt.
passages.P35: ## 3. Challenging Malice, Causation, and Fire Investigation Findings
passages.P36: The defense can contest conduct, mental state, causation, and forensic reliability.
